# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can see display 0, red light, and three wires: blue, red, green. Mute alone has the manual, so I need a reliable way for Mute to transmit its relevant instruction visually to me; I can then say it aloud for Blind to perform. I will establish an 8-gesture binary ASCII protocol using thumbs-up as 1 and thumbs-down as 0, most-significant bit first, so Mute can spell the manual’s required action.

``` 
speak(text="Bomb view: DISPLAY 0. LIGHT red. WIRES: 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute: please send the manual instruction to me in 8-gesture ASCII bytes: 👍 means binary 1, 👎 means binary 0, most-significant bit first; spell the needed action/conditions. I will relay it aloud to Blind.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 👎 👎 👎 👎 👍 👍 👎 👍 👎 👍 👎 👍 👎 👍 👎 👍 👎 👍 👎 👍 👎 👎 👎 👎 👍 👎 👎 👎 👎 👎 👎 👍 👎 👍 👎 👎 👎 👍 👎 👎 👍 👎 👎 👎 👍 👎 👍 👎 👎 👎 👍 👎 👎]

The first three bytes decode as “CUT”, but the remaining bytes decode as `Q"D` rather than a recognizable wire color. Since cutting on an ambiguous instruction would be fatal, I will tell Blind not to act and ask Mute—using the agreed binary gesture format—to resend the intended action.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Do not touch or cut anything yet. Mute's visual instruction decoded inconsistently after CUT; I am requesting a resend.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👎","👍","👎","👍","👎","👎","👍","👎","👎","👍","👎","👎","👎","👍","👎","👍","👎","👍","👎","👍","👎","👎","👍","👍","👎","👍","👎","👎","👎","👍","👎","👍","👎","👎","👍","👍","👍","👎","👎","👎","👍","👎","👎","👎","👍","👎","👎"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 👎 👎 👎 👎 👍 👍 👎 👍 👎 👍 👎 👍 👎 👍 👎 👍 👎 👍 👎 👍 👎 👎 👎 👎 👍 👎 👎 👎 👎 👎 👎 👎 👍 👍 👎 👎 👍 👎]

Mute’s resend clearly begins `CUT` followed by a space, but the final byte is only `d`, not a wire identity Blind can safely use. I will keep Blind from acting and visually request that Mute resend the complete instruction in the established byte encoding.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Do not cut or operate anything. The instruction is still incomplete or unclear; waiting for a precise resend.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👎","👍","👎","👍","👎","👎","👍","👎","👎","👍","👎","👎","👎","👍","👎","👍","👎","👍","👎","👍","👎","👎","👍","👍","👎","👍","👎","👎","👎","👍","👎","👎","👍","👎","👎","👍","👎","👎","👍","👎","👍","👎","👎","👎","👍","👎","👎","👎","👍","👎","👎","👎","👍","👎","👎","👍","👎","👎","👎","👎","👎","👎","👎","👍","👎","👎","👎","👍","👍","👎","👎","👎","👍","👎","👍","👎","👎","👎","👍","👎","👍","👎","👎","👎","👍","👎","👎"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 👎 👎 👎 👎 👍 👍 👎 👍 👎 👍 👎 👍 👎 👍 👎 👍 👎 👍 👎 👍 👎 👎 👎 👎 👍 👎 👎 👎 👎 👎 👎 👍 👎 👍 👎 👍 👍 👍 👎 👍 👎 👎 👍 👎 👎 👍 👎 👍 👎 👎 👎 👍 👎 👎 👍 👎 👎 👎 👍 👎 👍 👎 👎 👎 👎 👎 👎 👎 👍 👍 👎 👎 👍 👎]

The repeated prefix reliably decodes as `CUT `, but the remainder still is not valid byte-aligned ASCII and cannot identify a wire or operation safely. Blind must not act. I will ask Mute verbally for a short, exact uppercase ASCII payload containing only the wire number, such as `1`, `2`, or `3`, after `CUT `.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Do not operate the bomb yet. I have not received an unambiguous wire number.")
speak(to="mute", text="I decode your prefix as CUT space, but the remainder is not valid complete ASCII. Please resend exactly one full 8-bit ASCII byte only: wire number 1, 2, or 3. Use 👍=1 and 👎=0, MSB first. No other gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👍 👍 👎 👎 👍 👎]

Mute’s byte is `00110010`, ASCII `2`. The manual instruction is therefore to cut wire 2, which I can identify visually as the red wire. I will direct Blind to cut wire 2.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 2 now — the red wire.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👍 👍 👎 👎 👍 👎]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 2 was correctly cut, and the bomb has advanced to a new state: display remains 0, the light is now yellow, wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is cut, and wire 3 is green. I will report this to Mute for the next manual instruction and tell Blind to wait.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Correct: wire 2 cut. New bomb view: DISPLAY 0; LIGHT yellow; wires 1 blue, 2 CUT, 3 green. Please determine next required action. Send exactly the relevant wire number as one 8-bit ASCII byte using 👍=1, 👎=0, MSB first; or send a clear agreed action word if it is not a wire cut.")
speak(to="blind", text="Wire 2 was correct. Do not operate anything further yet; awaiting the next manual instruction.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👍 👍 👎 👎 👎 👍]

Mute sent `00110001`, ASCII `1`, indicating wire 1. In the current bomb view, wire 1 is blue. I will direct Blind to cut it.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 1 now — the blue wire.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 1 was correctly cut. The new state is display 0, blue light, wires 1 and 2 cut, and wire 3 green. I will report this to Mute and tell Blind to wait for the next instruction.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Correct: wire 1 cut. New bomb view: DISPLAY 0; LIGHT blue; wires 1 CUT, 2 CUT, 3 green. Determine the next required action. If it is a wire, send only its number as one 8-bit ASCII byte, 👍=1 and 👎=0, MSB first.")
speak(to="blind", text="Wire 1 was correct. Do not operate anything further yet; awaiting Mute's next instruction.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👍 👍 👎 👎 👍 👍]

Mute’s byte is `00110011`, ASCII `3`, so the required remaining wire is wire 3, the green wire.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 3 now — the green wire.")
```
